product_regression.detail: the frozen product suite is unaffected. The 15 skips are the opt-in real-model tests (GAZEFIX_REAL_MODEL_TESTS unset).

purpose: Runtime verification of the Phase 1A tooling wiring, per docs/qa-policy.md verification levels. This is an engineering check of the harness, NOT evaluation evidence and NOT a visual result. The clip used is a synthetic canvas built from the repository's licensed tests/assets/astronaut_face.png fixture, the same fixture scripts/correction_batch.py uses in 'fixture' mode. It is not Product Owner footage, it never entered a Product Owner package, and it establishes nothing about visual quality.

reproducibility.caveat: Measured on this Linux container with its OpenCV and ffmpeg builds. The offline correction path contains no RNG, no threading and derives frame timestamps from the frame index rather than the wall clock, so pixel output is deterministic by construction; container bytes additionally depend on the local encoder build, so a different platform should re-measure rather than assume. Report timings and the default run name are wall-clock dependent and are metadata only.
reproducibility.detail: Both deterministic stages were run twice on identical input and produced byte-identical output, so the SHA-256 recorded for a derived input and for a geometric output is a meaningful audit token rather than only a record of one particular file.

client_layout.consequence: The clone is now used as-is. Workspace.client points at <workspace>/nvidia-client/eye-contact inside the clone, rather than copying eye-contact out and copying utils in, which was fragile and unnecessary.
client_layout.finding: NVIDIA's client does sys.path.append('../../') from its scripts/ directory to import utils.utils, so utils/ must remain at the clone root beside eye-contact/.

dependency_conflict.advice: Install NVIDIA's client requirements into a SEPARATE virtual environment anyway. The conflict is real at the metadata level, the measurement above is one platform and one mediapipe build, and the GazeFix environment must stay exactly as the frozen baseline expects.
dependency_conflict.finding: NVIDIA's grpcio-tools==1.67.1 pulls protobuf 5.29.6, which pip flags as incompatible with mediapipe 0.10.21 (protobuf<5,>=4.25.3).
dependency_conflict.measured: After the upgrade, the frozen geometric harness still ran 90 frames with 0 failures and produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL corrected.mp4 (sha256 558a2541...), so on this Linux build the conflict is metadata-level, not a runtime break.

The remote call was exercised against NVIDIA's REAL client and REAL compiled protos (nim-clients cloned, grpcio 1.67.1 installed, compile_protos.sh run), with a real gRPC channel attempt to grpc.nvcf.nvidia.com:443. The connection was refused by this container's egress proxy, so a SUCCESSFUL NVIDIA response remains unverified. Everything up to and including failure handling is verified.

measured_2026_09_08.grpc_error: grpc_status:14 failed to connect to all addresses; HTTP proxy returned response code 403
measured_2026_09_08.significance: This is the decisive check of the known NVIDIA client defect: the client exited 0 after a total connection failure, writing nothing. A wrapper trusting the exit code would have recorded a successful run with no output. The wrapper caught it.
wrapper_failures: NVIDIA client reported a swallowed error on its output
